builds.name: Reference: Ranked bot core
builds.goal: Reference for Jinx: the core and runes ranked Emerald+ bot players use most (63,584 ranked Emerald+ games with this core on OP.GG, patch 16.20, 58.7% win rate).
builds.hypothesis: A ranged sustained-damage carry who swaps close attack speed for rocket range and splash, then accelerates after a takedown. Traps and Zap provide setup rather than reliable instant escape. The current adc provider core anchors this plan; later slots are observed options or reviewed kit completions. Core in purchase order: Hexoptics C44 → Runaan's Hurricane → Infinity Edge. Lethal Tempo keystone as played in those games. Remaining slots: Berserker's Greaves, Lord Dominik's Regards, Guardian Angel.
builds.summary: The proven bot baseline: Hexoptics C44 → Runaan's Hurricane → Infinity Edge, with Lethal Tempo.
testPlan: Play it in bot as your control build. Follow the purchase order; the core (Hexoptics C44 → Runaan's Hurricane → Infinity Edge) is what ranked players complete first.
Record kills, deaths, damage dealt and the minute you finish each core item, then compare other builds against these numbers in similar games.
Adapt the last two items to the enemy team: armor or magic resist against fed carries, anti-heal against healing, penetration once enemies stack resists.
failureConditions: Your results with this build fall clearly below the 58.7% ranked baseline over several games in the same role.
The enemy team composition makes the core items poor answers; swap the flexible slots before abandoning the core.
tradeoffs: Proven and predictable, so opponents know what to expect. It is a starting point, not the best build for every matchup.
The observed core and individual options do not establish six-item build statistics. Late slots are kit-based inferences.
Six-slot completion is our kit-based inference, not an observed six-item win-rate build.  Situational options replace an appropriate slot; they are not added as a seventh item.
buyOrder: Core in purchase order: Hexoptics C44 → Runaan's Hurricane → Infinity Edge.
Boots after the first item unless the lane needs them earlier.
coverageNotes: Source: OP.GG ranked Emerald+ solo/duo, patch 16.20, checked 2026-10-14. Core items and rune page are observed; later slots are observed options or reviewed completions. Win rates describe those games, not a prediction for yours.

kitEvidence.formula: Jinx fires a shock blast that deals [10 / 60 / 110 / 160 / 210 + (1.4) × AD] physical damage to the first enemy hit, Slows them by [40 / 50 / 60 / 70 / 80]%, and reveals them for [2] seconds.

Jinx tosses out 3 chompers that last for [5] seconds. They explode on contact with enemy champions, Rooting them for [1.5] seconds and dealing [90 / 140 / 190 / 240 / 290 + (1) × AP] magic damage to nearby enemies.

Jinx swaps weapons between Fishbones the rocket launcher and Pow-Pow the minigun.

While using the rocket launcher, Jinx's Attacks deal [(1.1) × AD] physical damage to the target and nearby enemies, gain [100 / 125 / 150 / 175 / 200] range, cost Mana, and scale [10]% less with bonus Attack Speed.

While using the minigun, Jinx's Attacks grant Attack Speed for [2.5] seconds, stacking up to [3] times (+[30 / 55 / 80 / 105 / 130]% %i:scaleAS% max).

Whenever a champion, epic monster, or structure that Jinx has dealt damage to within the last [3] seconds is killed or destroyed, she gains [175]% decaying Move Speed and [25]% Attack Speed for [6] seconds.

Champion takedowns stack the Attack Speed up to 5 times.

Jinx fires a rocket that explodes on the first enemy champion hit, dealing [20 / 35 / 50 + (0.12) × AD[statFormula=2]] to [200 / 350 / 500 + (1.2) × AD[statFormula=2]] + [25 / 30 / 35]% missing Health physical damage, gaining damage over the first second of travel time. builds.name: Zap artillery bruiser
builds.summary: Test zap artillery bruiser against conventional damage at equal gold.
builds.goal: Test zap artillery bruiser against conventional damage at equal gold.
builds.hypothesis: Zap carries 1.4 total AD physical damage and a strong two-second slow; Shojin supports repeated W/E and Cleaver assists physical poke. Earned Muramana adds spell physical damage while Eclipse offers a shield after separate hits; rockets remain an occasional safe finisher.
testPlan: Required state: Clear W sightline and enough mana after earning Manamune.
Compare W hit damage and casts over twenty seconds, plus a short attack phase.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Minions block W and missing crit makes sustained rocket attacks weak.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: No AP amplification of Zap and no automatic crit on W.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Muramana, Spear of Shojin, Black Cleaver, Eclipse, Edge of Night, Ionian Boots of Lucidity. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
coverageNotes: Only Cassiopeia Q/E and Sett W have numerical adapters. Even there, these other objectives and item/rune interactions may fall outside the model.
Proc inheritance, crit, pet hits and conditional helpers remain uncertain until observed. No completed mathematical maximum is claimed.

builds.name: Situational adaptation: Critical duel
builds.goal: Situational adaptation for Jinx: adapt to the specified fight rather than assume one universal build
builds.hypothesis: A ranged sustained-damage carry who swaps close attack speed for rocket range and splash, then accelerates after a takedown. Traps and Zap provide setup rather than reliable instant escape. Record minigun stacks versus rocket range and Get Excited state. Runaan and rocket splash must be tested together; takedown acceleration is earned, not permanently active. Crit attacks and a conditional shield test repeated duel windows.
builds.summary: Crit attacks and a conditional shield test repeated duel windows.
testPlan: Kit question for Jinx: Record minigun stacks versus rocket range and Get Excited state. Runaan and rocket splash must be tested together; takedown acceleration is earned, not permanently active.

Start with the early core (Kraken, then Navori if attack-driven recycling works) plus appropriate boots at matched gold. Record level, actual ability ranks, forms, resource and item transformations; six-item results do not establish lane strength. Use your intended lane or jungle role; jungle starters and early consumables are outside the final six slots.

Compare against the reference route at the same level, gold spent, finite stacks and opponent setup. Record unused gold; isolate an item change before changing runes. Run three repeatable trials of a short trade and a ten-second fight. Record damage actually landed, attacks/casts, misses, remaining resource and survival. Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.

Measure the actual interaction before granting item/rune procs: Crit attacks and a conditional shield test repeated duel windows. Test once stationary, then with a moving opponent and a fixed incoming damage pattern. Choose the opponent profile this defensive route is intended to address, then repeat against the wrong damage type.

Q evidence: Jinx modifies her basic attacks by swapping between Pow-Pow, her minigun and Fishbones, her rocket launcher. Attacks with Pow-Pow grant Attack Speed, while attacks with Fishbones deal area of effect damage, gain increased range, but drain Mana and attack slower. Keep finite champion/item/rune stacks explicit. Use Practice Tool, a custom match or your own replay; no numerical adapter is available for this champion.
failureConditions: A Lifeline slot excludes Sterak/Maw; melee access or ranged spacing must be earned.

The route fails Jinx's stated kit question: Record minigun stacks versus rocket range and Get Excited state. Runaan and rocket splash must be tested together; takedown acceleration is earned, not permanently active.
Higher dummy damage is offset by fewer landed actions, deaths before the useful window, or worse ally utility.
tradeoffs: A Lifeline slot excludes Sterak/Maw; melee access or ranged spacing must be earned.
Full cost 16,550 gold; delayed items, resource starvation and the two-item spike must be judged separately.
Counter-items are conditional. Change boots/defense for the real matchup, then record the modified setup.
buyOrder: Kraken, then Navori if attack-driven recycling works. Adapt component timing to lane/jungle pressure; do not blindly follow the displayed six-item order.
Keep appropriate boots while building the early core; swap boots only when the measured matchup justifies it.
Infinity Edge, Immortal Shieldbow, Lord Dominik's Regards are later or conditional slots; do not postpone necessary protection for a six-item ceiling.
Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.
coverageNotes: No numerical damage or survival adapter exists for this champion. Loading this proposal opens a manual test sheet, not calculated damage.
Source formulas remain in Champion kit. Symbolic values, unresolved tokens and helper records are evidence to inspect, not a certified executable simulator.
Legal source item/rune references were checked; retained map flags cannot prove every live-shop condition. Confirm shop eligibility, exact on-hit/on-attack rules and real proc cooldowns in game.

builds.name: Chomper hybrid trapper
builds.summary: Test chomper hybrid trapper against conventional damage at equal gold.
builds.goal: Test chomper hybrid trapper against conventional damage at equal gold.
builds.hypothesis: Flame Chompers has 1.0 AP magic damage and a 1.5-second root; hybrid Statikk and Nashor preserve attacks while Lich Bane supplies a magic packet after deploying traps. This tests E-led choke trades rather than claiming her physical rocket kit gains AP ratios.
testPlan: Required state: Arm traps in a choke and land attacks while the victim is rooted.
Measure one trap hit plus three minigun attacks versus ordinary crit damage.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Long E cooldown and easily avoided traps cripple the AP investment.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Each trap does not guarantee separate full damage or repeated root on one champion.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
